A_target.statement:
Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ with $m \perp n$.
Then:
:$\map \phi {m n} = \map \phi m \map \phi n$
where $\phi$ is the [[Definition:Euler Phi Function|Euler $\phi$ function]].

B_source.statement:
Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ with $m \perp n$.
Then there is a [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|ring isomorphism]]:
:$\Z / m n \Z \cong \Z / m \Z \times \Z / n \Z$

substitutions.the ring isomorphism: the isomorphism between residues modulo mn and the product ring
substitutions.the group of units of a ring: the residues coprime to the modulus
substitutions.the units of a product ring: pairs of units, one from each factor

derived.units correspond under a ring isomorphis: the units modulo mn correspond to pairs of units

validity_conditions: A ring isomorphism restricts to a bijection between the groups of units, since it preserves multiplication and the identity.
The units of a product ring are exactly the pairs whose components are units, so the unit group of the product is the product of the unit groups.
Coprimality of m and n is required for the Chinese remainder isomorphism to hold, and it is exactly the hypothesis of multiplicativity.
proof_plan: From the [[Chinese Remainder Theorem]], there is a [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|ring isomorphism]] $\theta: \Z / m n \Z \to \Z / m \Z \times \Z / n \Z$.

A ring isomorphism maps [[Definition:Unit of Ring|units]] to units.
Hence $\theta$ restricts to a [[Definition:Group Isomorphism|group isomorphism]]:
:$\paren {\Z / m n \Z}^\times \cong \paren {\Z / m \Z \times \Z / n \Z}^\times$

$\tuple {a, b}$ is a unit of the product ring {{iff}} $a$ and $b$ are units.
Hence:
:$\paren {\Z / m \Z \times \Z / n \Z}^\times = \paren {\Z / m \Z}^\times \times \paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times$
